title: Continuous Cech cocycles with finite ell-adic field coefficients are coboundaries
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extending nonarchimedean norm topology. Put $F=E$; in particular, $F$ is complete. Work in the profinite universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; a profinite set means a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space. Let $q:T\to S$ be any continuous surjection of profinite sets. For $n\geq0$ put $T_S^{n+1}=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in T^{n+1}:q(t_0)=\cdots=q(t_n)\}$ with the subspace topology. Let $C_n=C(T_S^{n+1},F)$, where $C(-,F)$ consists of all continuous functions, with pointwise addition [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Define $d_n:C_n\to C_{n+1}$ by
$$ (d_nf)(t_0,\ldots,t_{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j f(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{n+1}). $$
Then for every integer $n\geq1$ and every $f\in C_n$ with $d_nf=0$, there exists $g\in C_{n-1}$ with $d_{n-1}g=f$. The empty surjection is included. The assertion is about these actual continuous-function groups with values in the fixed complete field E, without replacement by locally constant functions.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2)–(4) and its proof, with G=1: discrete coefficients, sequential profinitely split inverse limits, and sequential closed colimits. Agent-formulated Cech consequence for finite E, obtained from O_E = lim O_E/pi^m and E = colim pi^(-m) O_E; not asserted for the noncomplete norm-topological algebraic closure. Blueprint motivation: main-20261015 direct-images proof paragraph (3), finite E branch.

proof.text: Give each positive coefficient quotient A_m the discrete topology. Apply lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower to identify the integers O_E, with their spectral subspace topology, with the compatible-family subring of the positive quotients. The quotient maps are additive and continuous; the transition maps are surjective quotient factor maps. Positive-level finiteness is the interface in def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension. The subring membership equations identify this limit with the compatible-sequence subtype used by lem-sfb-inverse-limit-cech-primitive.

For an integral cocycle h, project its signed-sum equation to every finite coefficient quotient. Apply lem-sfb-finite-coefficient-cech-primitive-lift with A the zero group PUnit and B the first quotient to obtain a first primitive. Apply lem-sfb-inverse-limit-cech-primitive with this prescribed primitive and compose the resulting continuous limit-valued primitive with the inverse of the ring homeomorphism. Injectivity of the ring isomorphism and equality in each coordinate prove the integral boundary equation.

The equal-image tuple space is closed in the finite product of T: write its condition as an intersection of closed equalizers. It is compact. The continuous image of f therefore has a positive norm bound R. The spectral norm makes E a nontrivially normed field; Mathlib supplies a nonzero scalar a with norm(a) < 1/R. The DVR theorem identifies O_E with the closed unit ball, so h=a f is a continuous integral cocycle. Solve it by the preceding step and multiply the resulting primitive by a^(-1). Distribute fixed scalar multiplication through the finite sums and cancel the nonzero scalar. This also works for empty tuple spaces and for n=0.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2)-(4), printed page 33. Existing finite primitive lifting and inverse-limit primitive declarations implement the discrete and sequential-limit steps. Mathlib compactness and norm bounds implement localization with one nonzero scalar.
